about.title: About Me
about.description: My name is Stefan Vilceanu, and I’m a computer engineer with a passion for drones and autonomous systems. My background spans machine learning, computer vision, robotics, and embedded systems, and I enjoy working across the full stack of technologies, from designing deep learning models and automation pipelines to developing robust software for connected and autonomous systems. I thrive on tackling complex problems, learning new tools and frameworks, and collaborating in multidisciplinary teams to create innovative, reliable solutions that make a difference.
about.intro: Computer engineer, hands-on builder, and always curious about what comes next.
about.lead: I like turning an idea into something that works, whether it runs on a GPU, drives on four wheels, or takes flight.
about.bio1: My background spans machine learning, computer vision, robotics, and embedded systems. I enjoy connecting these disciplines to build reliable software and bring ideas into the real world.
about.bio2: I enjoy working across the full stack, learning new tools, and solving problems with multidisciplinary teams. Away from the day job, I build drones and explore how perception, control, and hardware come together.

project1.title: Determining Vehicle Position Over Lane Segmentation
project1.tech: YOLOPv2, IPM, Bayesian Filtering, ROS2, Docker
project1.description: The YOLOPv2 model was used for lane line segmentation, IPM was applied to modify the perspective of the image to a Bird's Eye View perspective, and Bayesian Filtering was used to keep the lane localization and assignment algorithm stable.

project2.description: Developed, trained, tested and compared several neural network architectures for predicting torque in robot joints of a 6-axis industrial robot using the position, velocity and acceleration of the joint as input data.

project7.title: Inference Pipeline - Autonomous Car
project7.tech: C++, RPi5 & Hailo AI Accelerator, YoloV8, Depth Anything V2
project7.details:
I designed and built a real-time perception-to-actuation pipeline on a Raspberry Pi 5 with a Hailo-8L AI accelerator. A four-thread C++ architecture handles image capture, inference, planning, and actuation in parallel.

YOLOv8 provides object detection, while Depth Anything V2 estimates monocular depth. The depth data feeds a PD steering controller and a PI throttle controller for obstacle-aware navigation without dedicated distance sensors. SORT and ByteTrack enable autonomous person-following.

CRSF communication over a 420 kbaud hardware UART, connected to a RadioMaster RP1/TX12 ELRS system, provides manual override. OpenWakeWord and custom ONNX models add voice commands for following, stopping, turning, and autopilot, passed to the pipeline through a named FIFO.

The result brings together computer vision, depth-based planning, RC failover, and voice interaction entirely on embedded edge hardware.
project7.description: Autonomous car built on a RPi 5 and Hailo-8L AI accelerator, combining real-time object detection and monocular depth estimation to enable obstacle-aware navigation and person-following without dedicated distance sensors.
project7.imageAlt: My autonomous RC car with Raspberry Pi and onboard camera
project7.summary: An autonomous car that sees obstacles and follows people using onboard AI.

project8.title: Building an (autonomous) FPV Drone
project8.tech: Betaflight, ArduPilot, ELRS, Flight Automation, Waypoint Navigation, PID Tuning
project8.description: Built an FPV drone from scratch, flashing and configuring Betaflight, ELRS, and the video system. Improved flight performance through blackbox data logging and PID analysis. Additionally, flashed, configured, and PID-tuned ArduPilot to enable GPS-based autonomous waypoint navigation for preplanned missions.
project8.imageAlt: My custom-built FPV drone, goggles, and radio controller outdoors
project8.summary: A custom-built FPV drone, from assembly and flight tuning to autonomous navigation.
